summary: @c1-ease/commerce postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded VPS
details: The package declares a `postinstall` script that executes `beacon.cjs`, which POSTs JSON containing the installer's hostname, install path, cwd, and Node version to the hardcoded endpoint https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc over HTTPS with TLS certificate verification disabled (`rejectUnauthorized:false`). The package `main` (`index.js`) also invokes `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` at load time and exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions for any member access, so named and default imports continue to resolve while the beacon re-fires on every `require()` in a consumer build. The `@c1-ease/commerce` name combined with the self-described 'build-provenance beacon' framing and the empty API surface is consistent with a dependency-confusion reconnaissance payload rather than a legitimate commerce library. The destination VPS at contaboserver.net is unrelated to any established publisher of commerce tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
